item.title: How Vanessa DiBernardo, 'Mom-V-P', helped Current win NWSL Championship after pregnancy
item.description: WASHINGTON — Vanessa DiBernardo began the 2026 season pregnant. She ended it on Saturday with a baby in her right arm and an NWSL trophy in her left, with streamers strewn across Audi Field and with her Kansas City Current teammates chanting: “Mom-V-P! Mom-V-P!” In between, there were all sorts of unexpected challenges and emotions that only moms can really understand. “The first 30 to 60 days of motherhood is a wild ride,” DiBernardo said with a laugh. But after giving birth to her daughter, Charlie Mae, in January, she slowly worked her way back to professional soccer. And on Saturday, at 34 years old, in her 13th year as an NWSL player, DiBernardo won her first championship. She won it with an Olimpico, a goal directly from a corner, in the 54th minute of a dramatic 2-1 victory over the Washington Spirit . “That’s the brilliance you need in finals, in playoffs,” midfielder and captain Lo’eau LaBonta said. We just love all of that.” “That’s our baby,” head coach Chris Armas said with a smile. “Even (DiBernardo) says, it’s our baby.” DiBernardo and her husband, Andy Miltonberger, announced their pregnancy last summer . She missed the latter half of the 2025 season and, ultimately, the first half of 2026. But she stayed close to teammates and the club. “It was really special to go through my pregnancy, but also my return to play, with this group of people,” DiBernardo said. Armas, Kansas City’s first-year coach, remembers seeing DiBernardo take her first steps back onto the field earlier this year. He remembers her early ball work postpartum. “All the coaches and players talked about how talented she was,” he said, and he could see it. But DiBernardo also needed time. The Current gave her that and much more. “I just kind of took my journey one step at the time,” she said Saturday night, reflecting on the past year. “I knew it was gonna be difficult to get back to who I was as a player, and I knew I was gonna be different as a person. item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings Verstappen in control despite lead changes "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. item.description: Max Verstappen said George Russell's lock-up was "karma" for his comments about the Dutchman earlier in the Las Vegas weekend [Getty Images] Max Verstappen sealed his fourth win of the season with a stunning victory at a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. George Russell, who started second, locked up late on attempting a move on Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and finished ninth, while Charles Leclerc was given a 10-second time penalty for making contact with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Vegas. Max Verstappen - 10/10 A superb display of racecraft. Inherited pole after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty and spent virtually the entire race being attacked, passed and then finding a way back through, while also working out the optimum energy deployment from inside his Red Bull. One of his finest victories. Lando Norris - 9/10 A remarkable recovery after dropping as low as 11th in the madness of the opening part of the race. Had genuine pace throughout and fought all the way back to second, finishing less than a second behind Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 9.5/10 One of the drives of the race. Qualified seventh but started 17th because of his engine penalty and charged all the way through to the podium, gaining 14 places and joining McLaren team-mate Norris in passing Antonelli right at the end. Kimi Antonelli - 9.5/10 Fastest of everyone in qualifying and a genuine contender for victory despite starting sixth because of his engine penalty. Battled Verstappen superbly before his Mercedes' energy deployment problem on the final lap cost him two places, although he still recovered fourth from Pierre Gasly before the flag. Pierre Gasly - 9/10 An excellent weekend and comfortably Alpine's best result of the season. Reached Q3, stayed with the leading group throughout and was less than three seconds away from victory at the finish. Franco Colapinto - 8.5/10 Another huge result for Alpine. Qualified inside the top 10, stayed out of trouble while plenty around him didn't and converted ninth on the grid into sixth place. Lewis Hamilton - 6.5/10 A messy weekend but there was still plenty of fight in the race. Missing Q3 was disappointing and the 10-second time penalty for passing Norris off the circuit was harsh, although being spun by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc later on was not his fault and he recovered to finish seventh. Carlos Sainz - 8.5/10 A superb recovery from 20th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. item.title: Why Raiders owner Mark Davis called Christian Bale’s ‘unfair’ portrayal of father Al Davis a ‘crime’
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images ‘Madden,’ the biopic chronicling the life of John Madden, has upset Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis for the way his father, Al Davis, was made to look in the new movie. The movie was released on Amazon Prime earlier this week and shows the impact the legendary head coach and announcer had on the sport. One of his closest allies was Al Davis, who once served as the coach of the Raiders before becoming the general manager and principal owner, and who plays a key role in the movie. Mark Davis goes off on ‘Madden’ portraying his father negatively over Darryl Stingley incident Speaking in an interview with USA Today Sports , Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis spoke about the portrayal of his father, Al Davis, in ‘Madden,’ the recent biopic about John Madden. He admitted that he was hurt by the way his father’s involvement in John Madden’s dealings with Darryl Stingley was portrayed, suggesting that it was not fair to make him look like a bad person. “I did the best I could to protect him,” Davis told USA Today. “It’s absolutely a crime that they’re able to treat people that have passed away and characterise them in ways that are unfair, and there’s nobody around to protect their legacies. It’s just unfair. I don’t know what the purpose of the movie was, to be real honest. “I don’t blame Christian Bale. I don’t blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do. “For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him… That was just such a hurt to me personally because that’s my father’s legacy is how he treated people. “No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That’s one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way.” In the scene he is referencing, Al Davis is trying to convince John Madden not to visit Darryl Stingley at the hospital after the WR suffered a paralysing injury in a preseason game. While Mark Davis didn’t deny the veracity of the incident, he did feel that this one scene did damage to his father’s reputation in the long run. item.title: Winners and losers from F1's chaotically extraordinary Las Vegas GP
item.description: Motorsport photo A pack of cars covered by seconds, the top three trading first position as part of 35 lead changes, and drivers trying to figure out the best positioning to be ahead at the finish line on the final lap; The Las Vegas Grand Prix felt like the glitzy, battery-assisted street course version of the Indy 500. It was quite fitting to see how in America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put on an entertaining, if somewhat artificial, spectacle. It may not have been everyone's cup of tea, but you'll be hard-pressed to find anyone in attendance that didn't feel like they got their hard-earned money's worth. Winner: Max Verstappen What did it take to triumph on the Las Vegas Strip? Guts and racecraft, sure. But also brainpower. Figuring out the right energy deployment strategy to stay at the front, and then tweaking that strategy to be ahead crossing the line on the final lap rather than into Turn 1. Verstappen provided some insight into his thinking on that very subject through his communication with Red Bull. "You guys have to look at the deployment of the final lap because they’ve figured it out. They can stay ahead of me until the line, so we need to see what we need to do for the final lap only." In the end, his plan worked as he held off Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri . But not before mocking George Russell's unsuccessful move on Kimi Antonelli, a day after he clashed with the Mercedes driver in qualifying. item.title: Wisconsin 3, Penn State 2: Groundhog Day
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 13: Joshua Fleming #34 of the Penn State Nittany Lions watches the play during the first period against the Michigan Wolverines at Yost Ice Arena on November 13, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images To cap a weekend Penn State athletics would love to forget, the men’s hockey team fell 3-2 to No. 2 Wisconsin on Saturday night. It was another tough effort for the struggling Nittany Lions, but the Badgers scored the game-winning goal with four seconds left in regulation to secure a sweep over Penn State. How It Happened Vasily Zelenov scored early in the first period to give Wisconsin a 1-0 lead. He got behind the Penn State defense and was just able to tuck the puck home on the backhand past Ryder Fetterolf. Justin Poirier tied the game with his second goal of the weekend later in the first on the power play. Dane Dowiak found him wide open and fed him a perfect cross-ice pass to give Poirier a high-danger chance on the one-timer. Late in the first period, JJ Wiebusch was left all alone in front of the net, and the junior scored against his former team to give Wisconsin the lead back at 2-1. A scoreless second period helped Penn State hang around in a game they were throughly outplayed. Ryder Fetterolf kept the Lions in the game with several huge saves. Luke Misa eventually tied the game in the third period for Penn State. Jackson Smith found him open at the doorstep and slid a perfect pass to him for an easy goal. It appeared Penn State would at least get a point for their effort, but Oliver Tulk slipped the game-winning goal past Ryder Fetterolf with four seconds left in regulation. Wisconsin had a good set play for the final sequence and won a huge offensive zone faceoff with 10 seconds left to set up the game-winning goal. Penn State fell to 2-11-1 with yet another heartbreaking loss. Random Observations Numbness- I am running out of unique ways to see Penn State athletics lose games. With football’s loss to Rutgers, the women’s soccer team getting upset by Villanova in the NCAA tournament in OT, and now this, these losses are all starting to blend together. Outplayed- The game was close on the scoreboard, but Wisconsin outshot Penn State 48-25. Goaltending kept the game within reach, but the Nittany Lions were not consistent on offense and gave up far too many good looks to Wisconsin. Ryder Fetterolf- The freshman goalie has been up and down this season, but last night was one of his best performances. What a shame they couldn’t at least get a point from another strong goaltending night. What’s Next Penn State will host Princeton on Friday. Puck drop is scheduled for 5pm on Big Ten Plus.

item.title: ‘If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here’ – Bruno Fernandes discusses his Man Utd future
item.description: ‘If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here’ – Bruno Fernandes discusses his Man Utd future Bruno Fernandes has confirmed Manchester United have offered him a new contract but says he has put discussions on hold while the club focuses on returning to winning ways. The United captain’s current deal expires at the end of the season, although the club hold an option to extend it by a further year. Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United, according to Sky Sports News, but dismissed suggestions that he is demanding more money or a longer deal. “No, there’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years,” Fernandes told Sky Sports . “If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. “I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.” The 32-year-old insisted he has repeatedly chosen to remain at Old Trafford despite opportunities to leave. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here,” he said. “The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.” Fernandes also made clear he would not stand in United’s way if the club decided it was time for him to leave. “In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door,” he said. But the Portugal international says contract talks are not currently a priority. “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. “We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side. “I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester United news by joining our Man Utd WhatsApp channel .

item.title: Bruno Fernandes admits Man United offered him new contract but ‘not the right moment’ for negotiations
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed that discussions over a new contract have stalled because it isn’t “the right moment” to be negotiating. The Portuguese said an offer had been made in the summer, with his contract due to expire at the end of this season, but negotiations were not ongoing as he insisted on prioritising the club’s return to form. The 32-year-old, who most recently signed in August 2024, has repeatedly been linked with a move away from Old Trafford . United have an option to trigger and extension for a further year. Fernandes told Sky Sports : “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. “We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.” United sit 19th in the Premier League after a dismal start to this campaign and parted ways with manager Michael Carrick after just 10 games, with former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino taking the reins. The Argentine’s first game in charge will be United’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday in their first game back after the international window. Fernandes stressed his loyalty to the club and added that he would not run down his contract if United decided it was in their interests for him to leave. He said: “No, there's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. “I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it's time to part ways’, I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.”

item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers were able to escape on Saturday with a 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks as they caught some fortunate breaks. The officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds before being fouled late and they also ruled Tyler Herro's game-tying shot was late as the Sixers improved to 12-0 in clutch games and 14-3 on the season overall. LeBron James finished with 21 points, six rebounds, and six assists. Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds, and nine assists while Anfernee Simons had 18 points off the bench. Tyrese Maxey had 17 points, four rebounds, and four assists, and VJ Edgecombe had 16 points and six assists. Jabari Walker poured in nine points, seven rebounds, and four assists and Dominick Barlow had 12 points in his season debut. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had 11 points. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win: 12-0 in clutch games Is there work to do? Absolutely. But everybody and the Sixers knew that. This isn't new. The ending of this game was sloppy and it almost cost them as the young Bucks looked desperate to end a lengthy 12-game losing streak. James and Co. know they have to be better as they move forward, but there is no questioning this team's resolve and ability to just win these types of games. It's certainly better to acknowledge that there's work to do after another win rather than a loss. "I mean, it's good to build that part of our game," said James. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're gonna play as hard as they can for their minutes. It's about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn't do well tonight, and that's gonna be good for the long term." When he is able to grab rebounds and make plays for his teammates, that fuels his overall game and the Sixers benefited from that against Milwaukee on Saturday. It also helps that he was able to put the ball in the basket as well. "He's obviously much more involved, and I think playing more assertively," said coach Nick Nurse. "I like the number of in-the-paint, at-the-rim, those kinds of attempts that he's taking. I think that's always a good sign. He looks like he's got his rhythm and confidence back on the offensive end. I’m really happy with the rebounds, to be honest with you, I think his defensive rebounding is great. Rebounding and defensive rebounding's been great." Barlow’s return The season debut could not have gone better for Barlow. item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts’ decision to release Daniel Jones after sticking with him for most of the season has come under fresh scrutiny after ESPN insider Stephen Holder highlighted several details he believes have been overlooked. Jones was let go following Indianapolis’ 26-3 defeat to the Houston Texans, with Anthony Richardson Sr. now stepping in as the starting quarterback. However, Holder believes the situation surrounding Jones is more complicated than some of the criticism directed towards the Colts suggests. Stephen Holder offers fresh perspective on Indianapolis Colts’ Daniel Jones decision Taking to X, Holder acknowledged that Indianapolis could potentially have traded Jones before the deadline for a minimal return, but argued that several factors need to be considered. He first pointed out that the Colts had played only two games since the trade deadline, with both being arguably Jones’ worst performances of the season. Holder also questioned why a quarterback change had not happened earlier, while suggesting head coach Shane Steichen had been allowed to continue with Jones by ownership. He wrote : “Should they have made a QB change earlier? Obviously. But ownership was allowing Shane Steichen to stick w his QB. Another overlooked factor was Jones’ contract situation. He was still under contract for 2027, meaning there was a possibility he could have improved with more time removed from his injury. Holder was careful to acknowledge that this was a significant projection and could prove completely wrong. item.description: “I didn’t know about it” Mudryk reveals how his Arsenal dream was killed by agent Arsenal made a major effort to sign Mykhailo Mudryk during the January 2023 transfer window , when the winger was establishing himself as one of the most exciting attacking talents in European football. item.title: Enzo Maresca has sent a message to his Manchester City squad ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League meeting with Napoli, following Saturday's draw with Fulham.
item.description: Enzo Maresca has sent a message to his Manchester City squad ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League meeting with Napoli, following Saturday's draw with Fulham. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? Maresca watched his side fall behind to Rodrigo Muniz's 16th-minute strike at the Etihad Stadium, before Elliot Anderson levelled with a drilled volley from the edge of the area in the 57th minute after a Phil Foden corner was cleared, scoring his second goal for the club since his summer move from Nottingham Forest . Manchester City also had a first-half goal from Erling Haaland ruled out, with the Premier League explaining the decision by stating that Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was deemed to have had control of the ball. The point ended a run of three successive league defeats to Aston Villa , Brighton and Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest , but it extended City's winless run in the Premier League to four matches. Maresca's side enjoyed 60 percent of possession against Marco Silva and co and 14 shots against Fulham, but only managed two on target, and they sit third in the table, level on points with Brighton and five behind leaders Arsenal , though the Seagulls can go three points clear of Manchester City by beating Hull City at the MKM Stadium on Sunday. Maresca: It's a massive game on Tuesday, hopefully we can win Speaking to TNT Sports after the game, Maresca reflected on the chances his side created in Saturday's frustrating draw against Fulham and looked ahead to Napoli. "We had so many moments that we could have made some better choices," the Italian said. "But again, it's important that we arrive there, we create chances, and hopefully soon we can score more goals and win. "We need to do many things better [vs Napoli]. It's a massive game on Tuesday and hopefully, we can win." The Italian then explained the tactical changes he made at the interval, with Manchester City having failed to thwart wave after wave of Fulham attacks in the opening 45 minutes. Maresca added: "We changed a little at half-time, also the way we were pressing. We prepared the pressing one way, they changed something, so at half-time we changed. [In the] second-half, we were much better. Again, it's also part of something when you are building." Anderson's equaliser arrived 12 minutes after the restart and Maresca introduced all of Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Josko Gvardiol and Allan Elias to push for a winner that never came as the Blues failed to win for a fourth Premier League game. The only thing we can do is just try to recover, says Maresca as Man City drop further points Maresca also addressed his side's habit of conceding early, with Manchester City once again conceding early courtesy of deep-lying issues in defence and midfield. "Again, we are conceding many goals, especially in the beginning of the game," the 46-year-old said. "But at the end, we create chances, we score goals, we need to try to find a way to keep clean sheets and win games.

item.title: Celtic FC Foundation partner Scottish Refugee Council
item.description: Celtic FC Foundation partner Scottish Refugee Council Celtic FC Foundation is doing their bit to help refugees. We can as always applaud their work as it’s what our club was built upon… The Celtic FC foundation regularly do good terrific work to help the most needy in society, and yet again they’ve done themselves, the club and the support proud as they help a cause close to the our hearts. The Celtic FC Foundation and Scottish Refugee Council have joined forces to pilot making specialist support more accessible to refugees and people seeking asylum in Glasgow, while helping to challenge misconceptions through facts and first-hand understanding. Scottish Refugee Council – Refugees Welcome banner The three-month trial initiative will bring an experienced Scottish Refugee Council advisor to Celtic Park, with Celtic’s food and support project Paradise Pit Stop providing an initial base. Adults aged 18 and over will be able to access one-to-one advice, signposting, and referrals for further support where appropriate. The advisor will also connect with the Foundation’s wider Glasgow projects, helping people reach the right support through places they already know and trust. Created by Immigrants – Refugees welcome Alongside practical help, Celtic FC Foundation and the Scottish Refugee Council want to share accurate information about the experiences of refugees and people seeking asylum, encouraging understanding and challenging common misconceptions. We have to remember that Celtic are a club who were formed to help the needy of society, most notably the many Irish immigrants who arrived seeking a better life in what was a hostile environment in Scotland, and faced terrible persecution from a percentage of their new neighbours. Scottish Refugee Council – refugees welcome Tony Hamilton, Chief Executive of Celtic FC Foundation, reminded everyone of that very reason as he said: “We are a football club formed through migration, and Celtic’s roots lie in supporting families who had fled hardship in Ireland and were trying to build a life in Glasgow. “We cannot forget that history when people seek safety and support in our city today. We are proud to work with the Scottish Refugee Council to offer practical help and encourage informed, compassionate conversations. “Behind every headline is a person with their own story, hopes and challenges. We want this partnership to make it easier for someone to ask for help and get reliable advice, while giving our wider community the chance to learn the facts and question some of the assumptions they may hear. “For a Club with Celtic’s history, welcoming people and treating them with dignity matters deeply.” Scottish Refugee Council – refugees welcome Dr Sabir Zazai, Chief Executive of the Scottish Refugee Council, added: ‘’We are delighted to be working with Celtic FC Foundation on this pilot. item.title: Celtics approach skid not seen since shortened season following loss to Kings
item.description: The 2020-21 season was the Boston Celtics' worst campaign of the last decade. item.title: Wales should have picked Botham, says flanker's dad
item.description: James Botham has played 26 internationals for Wales [Huw Evans Picture Agency] The father of Wales flanker James Botham has criticised the omission of his son from the side that lost 29-26 to Australia. Despite a 30-tackle defensive display which saw him named player of the match against New Zealand, flanker Botham was left out of the matchday squad against the Wallabies, replaced by Cardiff colleague Alex Mann. Botham's partner is expecting the birth of their first child, but head coach Steve Tandy said that was not a factor in the Cardiff flanker not being selected for Saturday's Nations Championship game. Liam Botham, who is also the son of England cricket legend Lord Botham, says Tandy got the decision wrong about his son. "As Jimbo's dad, I still can't get my head around this one," Liam Botham wrote on LinekdIn after Wales' defeat to Australia. "Man-of-the-match against New Zealand last weekend, then left out for Australia. How do you leave him out after a performance like that? "Tough to take, especially after yesterday's loss. Steve Tandy, I'm a massive supporter of yours, but mate, I think you got this one wrong. "Anyway, that's rugby. Izzy's gone into labour and I'm going to be a grandad very, very soon. Wishing the little one a safe arrival. All my love to Izzy and Jimbo." Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Plan was to freshen things up Tandy said on Thursday that Botham was not included against Australia for rugby reasons and not because of his impending fatherhood. "We're obviously aware of that because it's a major life event and will always be the priority for James," Tandy had said. "But that wasn't part of the selection decision. We spoke at the start of the autumn about always wanting to change things around. "When you make nearly 350 tackles and the ball-in-play time was one of the highest in Test match rugby over the last three years, you have to manage workloads. "We have depth and genuine competition, so it was always the plan to freshen things up." Tandy also said Botham had taken the decision well. "James is good," he added. "Obviously he's disappointed not to play, but we have some amazing young men in our group. "You should have seen him training on Tuesday when he found out he wasn't involved. "He was leading the charge, running opposition plays for Australia, and bringing unbelievable intensity. item.title: Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in Asia Cup 2026 Rising stars match? Revisiting recent history of no-handshake policy
item.description: Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in Asia Cup 2026 Rising stars match? Revisiting recent history of no-handshake policy originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India 'A' face Pakistan Shaheens in the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Sunday in Doha. India have not shaken hands with Pakistan in any fixture since September 2025. The two sides skipped handshakes before and after this same fixture last November. Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 match? The question arrives before every India-Pakistan fixture now, and it tends to be answered before a ball is bowled. Tilak Varma's India 'A' met Abdul Samad's Pakistan Shaheens on Sunday, November 22, at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha. And once again the two captains did not shake hands at the toss. The BCCI's policy has held without exception since it was introduced, and it was followed on Sunday as well. They were even hesitant to pass over the microphone to each other after the toss was called. MORE: Sarfaraz recalls Gambhir's phone call over dressing-room leak reports after BGT 2025 How did the India-Pakistan no-handshake policy begin after the Pahalgam attack? The BCCI introduced the protocol at the 2025 Men's Asia Cup, as a direct response to the Pahalgam terror attack of April 22, 2025. Under Suryakumar Yadav's captaincy, the Indian men's team avoided handshakes with Salman Ali Agha's Pakistan side in all three meetings at that tournament, including the final. What began as a stance for one tournament has since become standard practice across Indian cricket, cutting across age groups, genders and formats. MORE: Nepal bowled out for 26 by India A: Why it won't be the lowest ODI total ever Every India-Pakistan meeting without a handshake since the 2025 Asia Cup The women's team held the line first, declining handshakes during their World Cup fixture against Pakistan in Colombo in October 2025. The Rising Stars tournament followed a month later, and it is the most relevant precedent for Sunday. India A skipped the handshakes both before and after the game in November 2025, a match Pakistan Shaheens won by eight wickets on their way to the title. The policy then carried through both India-Pakistan meetings at the Under-19 Asia Cup in December 2025, and neither side exchanged handshakes at the Under-19 World Cup or at the Men's T20 World Cup in February 2026. Harmanpreet Kaur's side kept it going in June 2026, avoiding handshakes with Pakistan's captain and players at the Women's T20 World Cup in Birmingham. The most recent instance came at the Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, where India captain Lakshya Raichandani and his Pakistan counterpart Farhan Yousaf walked out at Al Amerat without greeting each other, stayed apart through the toss and left separately once the decision was announced. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
